summary: Lower Parel (West), Mumbai-400013 .Petitioner - _(a) Hold and declare that the Petitioner is entitled to an extension of Financial Closure in the facts and circumstances detailed in the present Petition; and / or_ - _(b) Pass such other orders that this Hon’ble Commission deems fit in the facts of this case_ - _(a) Restrain the Respondent No. 1 from taking any coercive steps against the Petitioner, during the pendency of the present Petition._ f) The Respondent No. 1 sent an email to the Petitioner on 27.08.2025, whereby it has asked the Petitioner to confirm the date of achievement of the FC along with supporting documents under Regulation 11A of the GNA Regulations. - i) As per proviso to Regulation 11A(2) of the GNA Regulations, the Petitioner was required to submit proof of FC of the project by 11.09.2025. Given uncertainty about whether the Bidar Sub-station would be ready on time, proceeding with FC at that stage would have exposed the Petitioner to the risk of heavy financial loss. 4. During the hearing held on 18.09.2025, the Commission directed the issuance of notice to the Respondents. _2. The Petitioner is directed to submit, on an affidavit within two days, (i) the present status of its Dedicated Transmission Line (DTL), i.e., M/s Welspun Narmada Pvt. Ltd – Bidar PS 220 kV S/c line along with the line bay at the generation pooling station, which was under the scope of the Petitioner and (ii) specify the date upto which the Petitioner is seeking extension for the financial closure._ _3. CTUIL was directed to submit the following information, on an affidavit, within two days:_ _(b) Status of 1 no. 220 kV line bay at Bidar PS, which is required for termination of the dedicated line of the Petitioner._ _At the outset, the learned counsel for the Petitioner and the Respondent, CTUIL, jointly submitted that the matter be reserved for order, with the parties permitted to file their respective written submissions, if any._ _2. Considering the above, the Commission permitted both sides to file their brief written submissions, if any, within two weeks, with a copy to the other side. The interim direction issued vide Record of Proceedings for the hearing dated 26.9.2025 shall continue until a decision is taken in the matter._ _3. The Commission further directed the Petitioner to file the following information, on an affidavit, within two weeks:_ - _(i) In compliance with the Record of Proceedings for the hearing dated 23.9.2025, indicate the date up to which the Financial Closure extension is required and the reasons for the same._ - _(ii) Project Progress Status as per the format annexed with this Record of Proceedings._ - a) Despite the absence of the final grant of Connectivity and the Connectivity Agreement, the Petitioner has achieved FC through internal financing from group entities on 13.11.2025. The Petitioner has submitted proof of achieving FC to the Respondent on 14.11.2025 along with supporting documents, to which the Respondent has not responded. The Petitioner reserves the right to initiate further proceedings and/or take recourse to remedies available under law, if so necessitated with respect to the same. - c) Due to the subsistence of status-quo direction in the subject matter and the fact that this Commission’s Order will adjudicate on the treatment/ administration of the application, the subject development [request for withdrawal of application received from applicant] is brought on record. _At the outset, the learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the present Petition had been filed seeking an extension of time for the Financial Closure of the 250 MW capacity Wind-Solar Hybrid Power Project at Bidar, Karnataka. The learned counsel further submitted that the matter was reserved by the Commission after hearing the parties at length. However, the Respondent, CTUIL, subsequently mentioned the matter for rehearing._ _**The learned counsel further submitted that, vide its application dated 19.1.2026, the Petitioner requested CTUIL to allow withdrawal of its application for the grant of connectivity in terms of Regulation 3.7.3 of the GNA Regulations. Accordingly, nothing survives for adjudication in the present matter** . The learned counsel further sought a week’s time to file an affidavit placing the aforesaid aspects/developments on record._ _3. After hearing the learned counsel for the parties, the Commission directed the Petitioner to file its affidavit, as above, within a week, with a copy to the Respondent._ - b) CTUIL with submission dated 16.02.2026 stated that it would not be able to process the Petitioner’s application for withdrawal in view of the directions of this Commission vide ROPs dated 26.09.2025 and 30.10.2025 to maintain _status quo_ , and accordingly, the said application would remain subject to the outcome of the present Petition. - d) That during the pendency of the captioned Petition for extension of time to achieve FC, the Petitioner has achieved financial closure on 13.11.2025, albeit with a delay of 77 days, and that this remains the sole issue for consideration before this Commission as on date. The proof of achieving financial closure, along with supporting documents, was submitted to CTUIL/ Respondent No. 1 on 14.11.2025. In view thereof, it is prayed that this Commission may be pleased to consider the same and pass appropriate orders, as deemed fit. 15. We have considered the submissions of the Petitioner, Respondent and perused the facts available on record. 19. CTUIL with submission dated 16.02.2026 stated that it would not be able to process the Petitioner’s application for withdrawal in view of the directions of this Commission vide ROPs dated 26.09.2025 and 30.10.2025 to maintain _status quo_ , and accordingly, the said application would remain subject to the outcome of the present Petition.
title: Petition under Regulation 41 (Power to Relax) and Regulation 42 (Power to Remove Difficulty) of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Connectivity and General Network Access to the Inter-State Transmission System) Regulations, 2022 seeking extension of the Financial Closure of the 250 MW capacity Wind-Solar Hybrid Power Project at Bidar, Karnataka, where the in-principle connectivity has been granted on 22.07.2024 M/s Welspun Narmada Pvt. Ltd
